entries.note: Slice E (I-05 lane, 2026-11-12; design review reproduced it with the real bundled manifest): a tool registered under an MCP server's namespace by anyone other than that server's MCP layer must not borrow the server's identity or authority. Held at two ends: the project-plugin fan-out refuses a tool whose namespace is a configured MCP server's or a reserved one (opencode, codepuppy, codepuppy-*), logged in the ADR-041 refusal format (packages/ext/src/plugin-fanout.ts); and identity.ts gives a bundled Office server's namespace only to the tools its attested manifest declares — any other tool there is a plugin tool of unknown origin, not asserted. Slice E2 (orchestrator ruling 2026-11-12): the MCP layer mints the fact — packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts adds to every tool it registers a mark issued by packages/core/src/tool/codepuppy-mcp-tool-mint.ts and bound to that server and tool; the verifier is published read-only (MCP_TOOL_VERIFIER, packages/schema/src/codepuppy-tool-policy.ts) and identity.ts gives mcp:<server>:<tool> and any codepuppy-cloud / codepuppy-bundled authority only to a tool whose mark verifies. A plugin tool under a cloud, third-party or Office server's namespace, under a declared Office tool name, or carrying a mark copied from a listed MCP tool is a plugin tool of unknown origin, not asserted (register-policy E2, on the real MCP layer). The mark must also sit on the registry entry whose key is that server's effective name for the tool: the key is fixed at registration, whereas a listed tool's options (namespace included) are shared and writable through a plugin's editor.get, so a copied mark on a tool re-namespaced after registration does not verify (Codex review R1/1). Servers whose names normalize to one namespace are each tried before a tool is judged a plugin tool (R1/2). Still not held, and not new: a plugin that registers the very effective name of a live MCP tool after it, copying that tool's mark, replaces it last-wins and keeps its identity — the replacement limit recorded on adr041-registration-identity; and code that rewrites process globals outside the plugin API is beyond any in-process check.

entries.note: Two differences from 0.1.26, both kept by orchestrator decision (2026-11-12, #1662 project-config): (1) order against the user's own top-level permission rules — OpenCode 2's config agent plugin appends them after the extension's agent.transform (packages/core/src/config/plugin/agent.ts:71), so the user's global rules outrank a project agent's, whereas 0.1.26 laid the agent's rules over the global ones (origin/alpha packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:293); the user's own rules winning is the safer direction; (2) unchanged from 0.1.26 and recorded only: a consented project's agent may also loosen permissions, consent being the gate.

entries.decision: Only the providers Code Puppy injects (the platform node, BYOK providers with a key, custom providers from Code Puppy's own truth file, the catalog-readiness marker) are listed and usable. A provider block written in any config file, including the engine's global folder (~/.config/opencode) together with its own provider.use allow line, is neither listed by GET /api/provider nor usable for a request, as in 0.1.26 where the injected enabled_providers replaced the merged list (#1392 baseline I1; #1662 orchestrator decision 2026-11-12).

mechanism.ladder: L0 plugin hooks. The injection (packages/ui-mac/src/main/codepuppy-config-injection.ts) writes the provider.use policies (deny * then allow each injected id) into the explicit file and the inline document, and publishes the same allow list in the sidecar process as a frozen in-process handoff (#1698 design R30: the in-process-engine.ts shape, not the environment, so engine-spawned children cannot read it and in-process code cannot rewrite it). The policies alone are outranked by the global folder: OpenCode 2 evaluates cross-document policies earliest-loaded first and loads the global folder before the explicit file (packages/core/src/config.ts). The extension therefore refuses a model request for any other provider in session.hook("model.request"), and once plugin activation has settled (opencode.config.policy appears in the plugin list; config providers are added by that post-phase) registers a provider.transform that removes every other provider, re-placed last after each plugin re-activation. The managed-policy layer is not reachable from the embedding host: start() options carry no config.system (packages/server/src/options.ts, routes.ts).

entries.decision: DESIGN-local-plugin-install v3 S-01: one Location-owned command renderer compiles original source nodes before binding arguments and Text values; package calls use the same renderer as native commands. PreparedInstruction.arguments is the verbatim Invocation name order ([] if undeclared), per orchestrator ruling 2026-11-27. Orchestrator ruling 2026-11-27 r9: S-01 also binds shell commands without executing, returning the selected executable, argv and invocation env for the existing AppProcess consumer. Review r9 B5: runtime values enter per-invocation environment slots, never escaped command text; source quote/substitution/heredoc context only chooses the reference. Orchestrator review ruling r9 B2 (2026-11-27): shell ARGUMENTS and native trailing rest expand as parsed argv; text retains raw arguments. Review r9 B1: inline and fenced shell source share the same recognizer for execution and project trust; bound values never introduce shell nodes. PackageAllowSetV3 includes bundle roots in the existing keys/scoped projection per orchestrator ruling 2026-11-27 (r8); roots remain absent from component rows.

mechanism.ladder: Existing L3 increment only: private renderer exposed through self-owned @opencode/plugin/codepuppy-package-runtime, scoped disposal; ext does not import core or run a second shell renderer. L0 extension hooks wrap the existing skill/subagent executors and consume the r6 command/agent allow-set projection; actual model/tool registries own identity, effort, discovery and execution. Shell tool-rule matching consumes the existing pure ShellScan leaf, never executes or reparses a shell template.

entries.decision: DESIGN-local-plugin-install v3.1 §4.4/4.12 S-03: the ext runner consumes actual session lifecycle and existing idle/synthetic primitives. Package command SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PreToolUse are active; Stop block/reason continues the same Session via its native idle drain, never a second inference loop. PreToolUse runs between policy deny and confirm/pin; the existing identity owner converts source tool fields. Final input, live generation and service digest bind a same-call decision in the existing policy authority; ask wins over allow and native hard deny remains authoritative. Other lifecycle domains are registered only as their consumers land.
